title: Uniform geometric fibre bound for an etale scheme chart
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with atlas topology on field-valued point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A geometric point is a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ from an algebraically closed field [def-weil-geometric-point], and its geometric fibre is the sheaf fibre product with this map. Quasi-compact means quasi-compact on scheme tests, or, for a space, that every open cover has a finite subcover. Quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. Separated for a morphism means that its diagonal is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Etale means representable etale on scheme tests [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Integral means representable and integral on scheme tests [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; in particular its pullback to an affine scheme is affine. Open immersions are representable by open immersions on scheme tests [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $X$ be quasi-separated, let $U$ be a quasi-compact scheme, and let $a:U\to X$ be etale. There is an integer $d\geq0$ such that for every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ the geometric fibre $U_{\bar x}$ is a finite discrete scheme with at most $d$ points.

source.place: Tags 03JX (lemma-bounded-fibres), (eta) implies (delta), and 03JT (lemma-U-universally-bounded), finite affine covering of U.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $U=\bigcup_{j\in J}V_j$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] and quasi-compactness; allow $J=\varnothing$ when $U=\varnothing$. By [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence](1), $a:U\to X$ is a quasi-compact morphism: its source is quasi-compact and its target is quasi-separated. Consequently, for each affine scheme test $V_j\to U\to X$, the pullback $R_j=U\times_XV_j$ is quasi-compact. This uses only affine tests, so no quasi-separatedness of $U$ is being assumed.

The projection $p_j:R_j\to V_j$ is a morphism of schemes and is etale: it is precisely a scheme test of the representable etale map $a$, by [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $p_j$ is unramified. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points] to conclude that $p_j$ is locally quasi-finite. Thus each $p_j$ has a quasi-compact source and is locally quasi-finite, without any separatedness assumption.

source.place: Tags 02V5 (lemma-unramified-quasi-finite) and 02GK (lemma-etale-smooth-unramified), as in Tag 03WS (lemma-etale-locally-quasi-finite); spaces.tex Tag 02X2 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces).

proof.text: For each $j\in J$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-qc-source-bounded-fibres] to $p_j$ and choose a nonnegative integer $d_j$ bounding its finite fibre degrees. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound-field-points], for every field $K$ and every map $v:\operatorname{Spec}K\to V_j$, the scheme $R_j\times_{V_j,v}\operatorname{Spec}K$ is finite over $K$ and its ring of global sections has $K$-dimension at most $d_j$. Put $d=\sum_{j\in J}d_j$. The same finite sum works for all field-valued tests, and is zero for an empty cover.

Fix $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. The fibre $F=U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a scheme etale over $\Omega$, directly by the scheme-test definition in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] to $F\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ at the unique base point; its residue-field fibre is $F$ itself. Hence $F$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $\Omega$. Every such extension is $\Omega$: the minimal polynomial of any element is irreducible and has a root in $\Omega$, so is linear. In particular $F$ is discrete and every point of a nonempty $F$ gives an $\Omega$-morphism $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to F$.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), part (2), applied over an algebraically closed field; decent-spaces.tex remark-recall.

proof.text: If $F$ is nonempty, choose such $t$, and let $u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ be its first projection. Choose $j$ whose open $V_j$ contains its image; $u$ then factors through $v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V_j$. The fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies $F$ over $\Omega$ with $R_j\times_{V_j,v}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Explicitly, on a test $T\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, both functors consist of maps $z:T\to U$ satisfying $a\circ z=\bar x|_T$: the extra $V_j$ component on the right is forced to be $v|_T$. These mutually inverse identifications are natural in $T$ and preserve the structure maps. Step 3 therefore makes $F$ finite over $\Omega$ with $\dim_\Omega\Gamma(F,\mathcal O_F)\leq d_j\leq d$.

source.place: Tag 03JT (lemma-U-universally-bounded), comparison through scheme fibre products; the explicit pullback reassociation is the universal property of Tag 02X2 (spaces.tex).

proof.text: For nonempty $F$, finiteness over $\Omega$ gives quasi-compactness; the cover by its open point components from step 4 thus has finitely many components, say $r$. Each is $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Sections on this finite disjoint union form $\Omega^r$ by the sheaf gluing axiom, and the coordinate vectors give $\dim_\Omega\Omega^r=r$. Hence $\#|F|=r\leq d$. If $F$ is empty, it is the empty finite discrete scheme and has zero points, also at most $d$. This covers every geometric point and proves the assertion, including $U=\varnothing$ with $d=0$.

source.place: Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), final cardinality consequence, and Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field); elementary split-field calculation.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03JX and 03JT, using their scheme bounded-fibre input 03JA. Direct finite-affine-cover argument: apply spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 073B(1) to the chosen chart, then 03JA and 03J5 to U times_X V_j, and compare each nonempty geometric fibre using an Omega-valued lift.

The scheme theorem supplies local quasi-finiteness for etale projections; this is a geometric tool, not a different route for constructibility.
Tag 03JA is explicitly the scheme bounded-fibre input of the assigned Stacks 03JT/03JX route.

lean.statement: theorem exists_uniform_geometricFibre_bound {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hX : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X) (U : Over S) [CompactSpace U.left] (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (ha : IsEtale a) : ∃ d : ℕ, ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω) ⟶ S) (x : yoneda.obj (Over.mk s) ⟶ X.obj.obj), ∃ (F : Over S) (p : F ⟶ Over.mk s) (q : yoneda.obj F ⟶ yoneda.obj U), IsPullback q (yoneda.map p) a x ∧ IsFinite p.left ∧ DiscreteTopology F.left ∧ Nat.card F.left ≤ d
lean.note: The geometric fibre is a scheme representing the presheaf pullback, with its projection finite over the geometric field, discrete underlying topology and uniformly bounded point cardinality. Absolute quasi-separatedness is the existing affine-test criterion of def-sfb-space-absolute-quasi-separated; that landed definition node is added to stmt_deps. No change to the informal statement.
